subject: Re: Zenly evaluation \u2014 feature parity & next test plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenly.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Zenly evaluation — feature parity & next test plan

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: replace current hyperscaler inference for chat/assist product to reduce cost while meeting 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for 1–2k qps bursts.
- Must-have feature parity items: function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs (strict schema validation), streaming token-level responses for low-latency UX.
- Security/compliance filters & per-request response redaction are also required but can be handled in a post-processing layer.

Competitive notes we discussed
- You had already run Bedrock and Azure in earlier POCs; biggest gaps were streaming SDK behavior (partial tokens delivered), and fine-grained function-calling where you can assert strict output schema.
- Hyperscalers currently give good model coverage but you noted cost at scale and unpredictable throttling during bursts.

Immediate next steps (proposal)
1) Test plan: attached PDF (redwood-zenly-test-plan.pdf) with three scenarios: streaming chat, tool-calling roundtrip, and structured-output validation.
2) We’ll provide a sample schema and a small test harness (see attached schema stub) so you can run the same inputs you used against Bedrock/Azure for apples-to-apples comparison.
3) Dylan (cc'd) will lead a short technical walkthrough of our streaming SDK and function-calling contract; propose Wed 11/18 10:00am PT for a 45-min session.
4) We’ll run latency/throughput sweeps and share the latency-comparison.csv with percentile breakdowns within 48 hours of the test run.

Can you confirm:
- test window (we propose Wed 11/18 morning PT)
- list of endpoints/inputs you want us to include (or if you want us to re-use the BEDROCK test corpus you previously ran)

Attachments: redwood-zenly-test-plan.pdf, zenly-structured-output-schema.json

Thanks — I’ll set the walkthrough once I hear back.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenly.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zenly evaluation — feature parity & next test plan

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few things from our side: 

1) Wed 11/18 10:00am PT works for the technical walkthrough. Please add Priya (engineering manager) and I to the calendar invite.
2) For the structured outputs we need: a) deterministic schema validation (we must fail the call if schema doesn't match), b) explicit error metadata when validation fails (field path + reason).
3) Streaming: we need a hop-by-hop behavior doc — how do partial tokens appear, do you guarantee ordering, and how does reconnect/resume behave mid-response?
4) Throughput: we will run 1k sustained qps for 30s and then 2k burst for 60s. Please confirm any client-side batching recommendations you have.

Also, can you confirm whether you’ll run tests on the Redwood-hosted environment or a dedicated instance? We want to know if results include potential multi-tenant noise.

Appreciate it — attaching the Bedrock test corpus we used earlier so we can reuse inputs if possible.
— Alex
Alex Chen
Director of Platform Engineering, Zenly AI
alex.chen@zenly.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@zenly.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 07:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Zenly evaluation — feature parity & next test plan

Alex — great questions, answers below inline and attached a slightly expanded schema with failure metadata (zenly-structured-output-schema.json).

- Walkthrough / invite: I’ve sent the Wed 11/18 10:00am PT invite and included Priya. Dylan will demo a short streaming example and the function-calling roundtrip.

- Deterministic schema validation: Redwood supports strict output mode where the model output is validated against your JSON schema server-side; when validation fails we surface a structured error payload: {"error_type": "schema_violation", "field_path": "details.items[2].name", "reason": "type_mismatch"}. We included the schema that demonstrates both strict and permissive modes. (See attached schema stub.)

- Streaming semantics: partial tokens are delivered in order as we decode; we expose sequence numbers and an incremental 'delta' field so client can reassemble. On reconnect, clients can request resume from the last sequence number; the server will attempt to honor resume for the same request_id for up to 30s. I put a short behavior note in the test plan.

- Throughput notes / client batching: for the 1k/2k tests we recommend max client-side batch size of 8 and use our asynchronous streaming client to keep tail latency below target. We’ll run both multi-tenant (hosted) and dedicated runs

- you will get both datasets. Hosted runs will include typical multi-tenant noise; dedicated runs remove noisy neighbors.

Planned deliverables after the run:
- latency-comparison.csv with p50/p90/p95/p99 and time-to-first-token metrics
- raw trace samples for a few failed schema cases
- a short recorded demo of the streaming behavior for your engineers

Action items for us:
- Dylan: run the hosted + dedicated sweep and share the CSV within 48h of the run.
- Rachel: please prepare a short sample that demonstrates strict schema rejection and error payloads (attachable to the PR).

Let me know if anything else — we’ll start the runs right after the walkthrough.

Best,
Marissa

Team — quick internal note after repeating the answers to Alex. High priority: get the hosted + dedicated sweep scheduled immediately after the 10:00am PT walkthrough.

Notes / asks:
- Dylan: lead the walkthrough + run the sweeps. For the dedicated run, provision a 4xA100 equivalent pool (we want to minimize model variance between infra providers). Target: p95 <= 350ms for the 1k sustained test; keep the p99 as low as viable.
- Rachel: prepare the rejection demo and a couple unit tests that assert the error payload fields we discussed (field_path + reason). Attach brief sample to the shared Drive link I added in HubSpot.
- Jonas: FYI — Zenly is evaluating Bedrock/Azure currently. They care a lot about predictable latencies and strict schema enforcement. If we can show both hosted and dedicated numbers, this will be a good competitive narrative vs hyperscalers.

Deliverables timeline:
- Walkthrough scheduled: Wed 11/18 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent)
- Sweep results + CSV: aim to share by Fri 11/20 EOD PT
- Demo/video + schema unit tests: by Fri 11/20 EOD PT

I’ll coordinate the HubSpot updates and attach the test artifacts there.
